Sanft's comments indicate the defense team views the conviction as a setback they intend to contest through the appellate system.

The case carries broader implications for how long-standing unsolved murders in the music industry are eventually resolved. With an appeal now underway, the legal proceedings surrounding Tupac's death are likely to extend further, keeping the case in public view and potentially influencing how future decades-old cases are prosecuted.

title: Watch Katseye Kick Off Wildworld Tour in Dublin
summary: The global trek will hit the U.K., Europe, and North America before wrapping in November

articleBody:
Katseye is hitting the road. The Los Angeles-based girl group has announced the Wildworld Tour, which launches in Dublin before traveling across the United Kingdom, Europe, and North America through November, according to Rolling Stone.

The six-member ensemble—Daniela Avanzini, Lara Raj, Manon Bannerman, Megan Skiendiel, Sophia Laforteza, and Yoonchae Jeung—brings a genuinely international composition to their performances. With members hailing from the Philippines, South Korea, Switzerland, and the United States, Katseye embodies the model of a global girl group, pooling talents and perspectives from across continents.

The Wildworld Tour represents a substantial undertaking for the group, stretching across multiple regions and months. Beginning in Dublin positions the tour in a key European market before the band moves through other European cities and eventually crosses the Atlantic to North America. The tour's conclusion in November suggests an ambitious schedule designed to build momentum heading into the final months of the year.

For an emerging act, a tour of this scope signals confidence in both the group's material and their fanbase. Touring requires significant logistical coordination and financial investment, and a multi-continent journey indicates that Katseye's label and management see viable audiences in each region. The European leg carries particular weight, as international expansion often determines whether groups can sustain long-term careers beyond their home markets.

The announcement comes as girl groups continue to dominate global pop markets. Katseye's international makeup aligns with a broader shift toward ensemble acts that reflect the borderless nature of modern pop fandom, where audiences connect across continents through streaming and social media. The Wildworld Tour will be crucial in translating that digital connection into live ticket sales and in-person fan engagement.

title: Sean Ono Lennon Confirms Birth of Baby Boy, John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s First Grandchild
summary: The couple shared the happy news on social media
whatHappening: Sean Ono Lennon has announced the birth of his baby boy, marking the arrival of John Lennon and Yoko Ono's first grandchild. The musician shared the news with fans via social media.
whoInvolved: Sean Tarō Ono Lennon is a British and American musician and son of The Beatles founder John Lennon and artist Yoko Ono. John Lennon, who died in 1980, was the co-lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist of The Beatles, whose songwriting partnership with Paul McCartney remains the most successful in history.
whyMatters: The birth extends the Lennon family legacy to a new generation and provides a personal milestone for Sean Lennon, a musician in his own right who has released three solo albums and performed with multiple bands. The announcement represents a symbolic continuity of one of popular music's most influential families.
articleBody:
Sean Ono Lennon has announced the birth of his first child—a baby boy—representing the first grandchild of the late John Lennon and Yoko Ono. According to Rolling Stone, the couple shared the happy news on social media, though additional details about the birth remain limited at this time.

Sean Tarō Ono Lennon, 49, is a British and American musician who has built a substantial career independent of his family's towering legacy. Over the course of his career, he has been a member of multiple bands including Cibo Matto, the Ghost of a Saber Tooth Tiger, and the Claypool Lennon Delirium, in addition to performing with his parents' group, Plastic Ono Band. As a solo artist, he has released three albums: Into the Sun (1998), Friendly Fire (2006), and most recently Asterisms (2024).

Sean is the son of John Lennon, the English musician and songwriter who gained global fame as the founder and co-lead vocalist of The Beatles, and Yoko Ono, an artist and activist. John Lennon died in 1980, decades before the birth of his first grandchild. Sean is the half-brother of Julian Lennon and Kyoko Cox, making him a bridge between different chapters of his parents' lives and legacies.

The birth of Sean's son extends the Lennon family line into yet another generation, providing a personal milestone for the musician as he continues his own creative work. The announcement comes at a time when Sean remains active in music production and performance, maintaining the artistic tradition that has defined his family for decades. The news represents a moment of personal joy for the Lennon and Ono families, shared publicly with their followers through social media.

title: Alanis Morissette Sues Former Tour Manager, Alleges ‘Extortionate’ Threat Over Airport Drugs
summary: The singer's new lawsuit claims she is "the victim of a calculated blackmail campaign"
whatHappening: Alanis Morissette has filed a lawsuit against her former tour manager, accusing him of running a blackmail scheme that allegedly involved threats related to drugs at an airport. According to Rolling Stone, the singer claims she is "the victim of a calculated blackmail campaign."
whoInvolved: Alanis Morissette is a Canadian-American singer-songwriter who became a cultural phenomenon in the 1990s and has sold over 60 million records worldwide, earning seven Grammy Awards among numerous other accolades. The lawsuit names her former tour manager, though the individual's identity and background details are not specified in the available information.
whyMatters: The case raises questions about power dynamics and potential misconduct within the music industry's touring infrastructure, an area where managers wield significant influence over artists' professional and personal lives. If proven, it could set precedent for how similar blackmail allegations are handled and may prompt greater scrutiny of tour management practices and safeguarding protocols.
articleBody:
Alanis Morissette is taking legal action against her former tour manager in a lawsuit that alleges an "extortionate" blackmail campaign, according to Rolling Stone. The singer claims her ex-manager threatened her over an incident involving drugs at an airport, leveraging the threat to extract something of value—a classic blackmail framework that the lawsuit characterizes as calculated and deliberate.

The specifics of what the manager allegedly sought in exchange for his silence, and the precise nature of the airport incident, remain unclear from the available details. However, the formal filing suggests Morissette's legal team has documented evidence sufficient to support the blackmail allegation in court. Blackmail cases in the entertainment industry are relatively rare at this scale, making the lawsuit noteworthy within celebrity legal disputes.

Morissette, who rose to international fame in the 1990s as the "Queen of Alt-Rock Angst," built her career on confessional songwriting and an emotive mezzo-soprano voice that resonated with millions worldwide. Her commercial success—over 60 million records sold globally—and her seven Grammy Awards, a Brit Award, and fourteen Juno Awards underscore her stature in popular music. A figure of this prominence making such allegations against a member of her touring infrastructure highlights the vulnerability even successful artists can face to exploitation by trusted associates.

Tour managers occupy a uniquely powerful position in an artist's life and career. They oversee logistics, finances, scheduling, and day-to-day operations during months-long touring schedules, often becoming confidants and quasi-advisors. When that trust is breached through blackmail, it strikes at both the professional relationship and the personal security of the artist. The lawsuit's framing as a "calculated" campaign suggests premeditation rather than opportunistic conduct.

The case will likely proceed through civil court, where Morissette would seek damages for the harm caused by the alleged extortion. Depending on jurisdiction and evidence presented, the matter could also draw attention from law enforcement if criminal charges are warranted. For now, the lawsuit stands as a public record of the allegation, adding another chapter to the ongoing conversations about accountability and power imbalances within music industry professional relationships.

title: Yeah Yeah Yeahs Unveil Live Album Recorded at London’s Royal Albert Hall

whatHappening: Yeah Yeah Yeahs has released a live album capturing their performance at London's Royal Albert Hall. The record, titled Hidden in Pieces Live at the Royal Albert Hall, was recorded last year and debuted alongside a short film.

For fans, the live album and accompanying film offer an intimate look at the group's energetic performance style that helped define their reputation during the 2000s garage rock and post-punk revivals.
articleBody:
Yeah Yeah Yeahs has unveiled a new live album documenting their performance at one of London's most prestigious concert venues. Hidden in Pieces Live at the Royal Albert Hall captures the New York indie rock band in concert at the historic 5,272-seat hall, which sits on the northern edge of South Kensington. According to Rolling Stone, the album arrived alongside a short film, offering fans a multimedia experience of the performance recorded last year.

The band, formed in 2000 by vocalist Karen O, guitarist Nick Zinner, and drummer Brian Chase, rose to prominence during the 2000s garage rock and post-punk revivals. Their evolution from the garage rock scene to their current status has been marked by their distinctive sound and electrifying live performances. The choice of the Royal Albert Hall as the venue for this live recording reflects the band's standing in contemporary music and their continued ability to draw audiences to major concert halls.

Live albums have become an increasingly important medium for established acts to document their artistry and connect with both longtime fans and new listeners. The inclusion of a short film alongside the audio release expands the project beyond traditional concert recordings, allowing viewers to experience the visual dimension of the band's performance alongside the music.

The release demonstrates Yeah Yeah Yeahs' sustained presence in the music landscape years after their initial breakthrough. By capturing a live performance at a world-renowned venue and pairing it with visual documentation, the band is preserving a specific moment in their ongoing career while also providing fans with a tangible connection to their live experience.

title: Watch Drake Perform ‘Iceman’ Tracks Live at Don Toliver’s Toronto Show
summary: The rapper showcased “Shabang,” “Burning Bridges,” and “Janice STFU" on stage for the first time
whatHappening: Drake made a surprise appearance at Don Toliver's Toronto show, performing three tracks from the upcoming 'Iceman' project for the first time live. The rapper debuted "Shabang," "Burning Bridges," and "Janis STFU" on stage, marking the songs' first public performance.
whoInvolved: Drake is a major Toronto-based rapper, while Don Toliver is an American rapper and singer from Houston signed to Cactus Jack Records, the label founded by fellow Houston artist Travis Scott. The two artists collaborated on the Iceman project, which Drake showcased during Toliver's performance in his hometown.
whyMatters: This live debut signals momentum building toward the official release of the 'Iceman' material and demonstrates the collaborative relationship between Drake and Toliver. The choice to premiere the tracks at a Don Toliver show in Toronto adds cultural weight to both artists' profiles and gives fans their first official listen to new music.
articleBody:
Drake took the stage unexpectedly at Don Toliver's Toronto show to debut three previously unheard tracks from the 'Iceman' project. According to Rolling Stone, the rapper performed "Shabang," "Burning Bridges," and "Janis STFU" live for the first time, giving the audience an exclusive first listen to the forthcoming material.

The appearance marked a significant moment for both artists involved. Don Toliver, the Houston-based rapper and singer who signed to Cactus Jack Records in a joint venture with Atlantic Records following a guest appearance on Travis Scott's 'Astroworld' album, has been building momentum as a rising figure in hip-hop. Drake's decision to collaborate on the 'Iceman' project and personally debut the tracks at Toliver's show underscores the strength of their working relationship and mutual respect within the industry.

The live performance served as a public unveiling of music that fans had been anticipating. By choosing to premiere the tracks at a Don Toliver concert in Toronto—Drake's own hometown—the artists created a significant moment for both fanbases. The three songs performed each offered different sonic territory, allowing listeners to get a full sense of the project's range and creative direction.

This type of surprise debut has become an effective strategy for building anticipation around new music. Rather than relying solely on studio releases or streaming announcements, the live performance created a memorable, shareable moment that would resonate with both attendees and fans following the news online. The fact that the songs were performed in Toronto, a city deeply connected to Drake's identity and career, added additional resonance to the event.

As anticipation builds for the official 'Iceman' release, this live debut provides a concrete preview of what listeners can expect. The three tracks performed suggest a project with distinct production styles and lyrical approaches, indicating that Drake and Toliver have put considerable thought into the creative direction of their collaboration.
